parameters.content:
## Google Calendar <-> Postgres Synchronization

Reusable sub-workflow. Input: syncCalendarId -- an internal id
referencing a row in sync_calendars. The real Google Calendar id
and API host are never caller-supplied; both come from that row
and a fixed host.

Phase 1 (loop): pull-sync via events.list, paginated, cursor-
advanced atomically per page inside process_page. A 410 Gone
resets to a full resync and restarts the loop.

Phase 2: drains sync_outbox (Postgres -> Calendar creates/
updates/cancels), idempotency-checked via a stable client-
generated key before any create, conditional (If-Match) before
any update.

A row-based lease (not pg_advisory_lock -- see docs) ensures
only one runner touches a given calendar at a time, and self-
heals on TTL if a runner crashes without releasing.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { status: 'rejected', reason: 'invalid_sync_calendar_id' } }];
return [{ json: { status: 'lease_busy' } }];

const s = $('Classify Fetch Result').first().json;
return [{ json: { ...s, isFullSync: true, pageToken: null, syncToken: null } }];
return [{ json: $('Build Calendar Error Response').first().json }];
return [{ json: $('Build Aborted Response').first().json }];

const j = $json;
return { json: { ...j, qs: { privateExtendedProperty: `idempotencyKey=${j.idempotencyKey}` } } };

const r = $('Accumulate Outbox Results').first().json;
return [{ json: { status: 'ok', pull: r.pull, outbox: r.outbox } }];
